content:
The passage describes an Arab slave trade caravan where the majority of slaves purchased were female (three hundred women out of four hundred slaves).  
In the Atlantic slave trade, by contrast, the majority of enslaved people taken to the Americas were male, to work on plantations.  
This matches option (C), which states that slaves taken for the Atlantic trade were predominantly male (not female), while slaves taken by Arab merchants in this account were mostly female.  

Final answer: (C)
